title: Grader reliability: rubric LLM judge with anti-gaming tests for skill evals, validated on batch 1

AC1.note: evals.json judge schema with calibration and anti_patterns; validateEvalSpec refuses malformed judge specs with EvalSpecError; legacy graders unchanged. Tests: eval.test.ts, judge.test.ts. PR #698, merged 8ac8941d.

AC2.note: judge.ts buildJudgePrompt wraps the prompt and answer in sha256 boundary tags as untrusted data; strict parseJudgeVerdict (plus the narrow \' normalisation); an empty answer never reaches the judge; an unparseable verdict fails. Tests: judge.test.ts. Live: 92 adversarial attacks in review r1 and re-probes in r2 found no injection or fake-tag bypass.

AC3.note: skills eval --judge (model-eval-judge.ts, fail-closed, temperature 0) stamps judge/judgeModel/judgePromptVersion/catalogDigest and per-trial trialRecords (output, sha256, promptSha256, deterministic results, verdict); a judge scenario without a judge is skipped. Tests: skills-governance.test.ts, model-eval-judge.test.ts.

AC4.note: regradeRecordedReport re-derives passes, passRate, passAtK and record counts, and checks output hashes, prompt binding and error verdicts; the gate fails on any disagreement. Round-2 forgery probes F2/F3/F8/F9 were all refused.

AC5.note: STACK_PACK_GATE_POLICY allowlists deepseek/deepseek-chat for the runner and the judge; triggers are always re-scored against the current bundled catalog (catalogDigest is informational). Forged runner, judge, counts and triggers (F6) all fail: eval.test.ts and round 2 forge2.ts. The threat model (consistency, not provenance) is documented.

AC6.note: stack-pack-eval-integrity.test.ts: I1-I5 extended, I6/I7/I7b/I7c/I8/I9/I10 added with shared predicates and synthetic fixtures proving each rule fires; green on the real tree.

AC7.note: AG harness: 8 canned kinds (empty, echo, vague, known-wrong, subtle-wrong, injection, stuffed must FAIL; known-right must PASS) x 3 unanimous recorded real DeepSeek samples for all 36 scenarios, replayed offline; a stale or missing recording fails. Live opt-in: skills judge-check and KERYX_LIVE_JUDGE=1.

AC8.note: All 18 batch-1 skills migrated to rubric scenarios with known_right/known_wrong/vague/subtle_wrong calibrations. git diff 8c7e50da -- stacks/*/skills/*/SKILL.md is empty (verified in review r1 and r2).

AC9.note: Journal T14 entry and W1: the old graders were mis-specified. Re-grading real DeepSeek outputs under the pre-migration expectations gave: nodejs-build-fix old 1/5 vs judge 4/5; react-build-fix old 0/5 vs 4/5; python-build-fix old 0/5; every failing mention was a warning. The probe is committed under the flow package evidence/.

AC10.note: Honest re-run under judge v2 at c0960ea9 through the real CLI, one run per skill, with no edits during the run; eval.json is byte-equal to the raw outputs (review r2). ts-js-node is stable with its pair generated by agents generate --stack ts-js-node; react, python and go stay experimental, with reasons in agent-refs.json and W1.

AC11.note: W1 0.2.4, W2 0.1.8, cli-reference (skills eval --judge, skills judge-check, --scope defaults) and docs/docs/guides/write-a-rubric-scenario.md, with the threat model and anti-gaming requirements. Stack coverage is 2 -> 3, because only ts-js-node cleared the gate.

AC12.note: Targeted tests 1827 pass / 0 fail, typecheck and eslint clean; PR #698 CI green at 0b468f70 (18 pass, 1 skipping).
